title: Broken Meridian - PS2-era arcade flight combat built with Claude Code, local TTS, Suno and image gen
author: KashinHS
selftext:
This is the teaser for Broken Meridian, an arcade flight-combat game I'm making for mobile. It's in active development and not for sale yet.

It's inspired by PS2-era Ace Combat (kind of obviously), but the whole campaign is a little more centralized and intimate, taking place on (or rather over) one island. Where you bring a bomber down matters: over the sea is fine, over a town is not. You cover a wingman, deal with an enemy ace squadron, and try evading missiles. Five missions are playable so far.

**Who does what**

* **Code:** Claude Code writes nearly all of it, including the tooling around the game. I do the game and mission design, the story, direction and playtesting, and I decide what stays.
* **Engine:** Godot 4.
* **3D:** Blender, but nothing is modelled by hand. Every model is a Python script Claude wrote, rendered in headless mode. No generative 3D.
* **2D art:** ChatGPT image gen. To keep the aircraft consistent I render my own Blender models and use the renders as references. No paint-over.
* **Music:** Suno.
* **Voices:** local TTS on a Mac via mlx-audio. Qwen3-TTS designs each voice from a text description, then VoxCPM2 clones that voice and speaks every line.
* **Not AI:** the terrain is procedural, the SFX are partly synthesised in code and partly recordings from the free Sonniss GDC bundles, and the font is Barlow Condensed.

**The voice pipeline**

There are 442 voiced radio lines across 28 voices so far. To manage that, Claude built me a small local web app I call Story Studio. I write a scene there, give each line a speaker and an optional delivery direction ("Measured and tired", "Dry, quietly relieved"), and it generates takes on several seeds. I audition them and approve one per line. Approving compiles the dialogue into the game and swaps in the audio.

The directions are why I moved every voice to VoxCPM2. With Qwen3-TTS, a direction made the voice drift into someone else. VoxCPM2 mostly (!) keeps the cloned voice and only changes the delivery although you can still hear a slight drift there. In the end I will probably need to move to something like Elevenlabs for a more consistent voiceover.

**What didn't work**

Local TTS is flaky, and the delivery can feel stiff even on the takes I keep. Everything else has mostly been normal iteration so far, nothing out of the ordinary,

**Why all AI**

Paying for human-made art, music or voices isn't realistic for me (even though I would really like to do that). So part of the point is to see how far I can get with the tools I have

Trailer on YouTube: [https://youtu.be/q59IU6PU5n4](https://youtu.be/q59IU6PU5n4)

Any feedback is welcome, whether that's the voices, the trailer, the game itself or anything else. And yes, my hype for Ace Combat 8 was the catalyst for me to try my hands on this project. I wanted to do that since my RPG Maker 2000 days in the now ancient past :D
